newsitem.title: UK: British public sector borrowing in line with forecasts.
newsitem.headline: British public sector borrowing in line with forecasts.

text.p: Britain on Tuesday issued public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) figures for November of 2.6 billion pounds ($4.31 billion), close to average analysts' forecasts of around 2.7 billion.
And the treasury said the figures were fully in line with government forecasts of a 26.4 billion pound borrowing requirement for 1996-7.

Gerard Lyons of DKB International told Reuters Financial Television: "This is the best PSBR for the past five years for this year to date. The economy is gathering steam and generating more revenues. Expenditure still needs to be kept under tighter control but that's difficult in the run-up to elections. The government can certainly meet their target for this year."
And David Philpotts of Schroders agreed "They're in line with expectations and the trend for the year to date is quite encouraging. The PSBR is well on course for hitting the Treasury's target."
